items.title: Exclude failed/pending assistant placeholders from the chat history sent to the model
items.body:
## Problem
`ChatService.claim` builds the history for a turn with `priorMessages.filter((m) => m.id !== message.id).map(...)` (`bridge/apps/backend/src/chat/chat.service.ts:142-144`). It drops only the message being claimed. Assistant placeholders are created with `content: ''` and `status: Pending` (`chat.service.ts:83-88`), and `failTurn` leaves a failed one with empty content (`chat.service.ts:179-190`). Those rows stay in every later turn's history. Providers such as Anthropic reject empty assistant content, so one failed turn can make every later turn in that chat fail. Related: `completeTurn` and `failTurn` (`chat.service.ts:166-190`) never check that the message is still `Running`, so a late or duplicate report can overwrite a completed reply.

## Proposed change
- In `claim`, keep only messages whose `status === ChatMessageStatus.Complete`. The claimed message is already excluded.
- In `completeTurn` and `failTurn`, throw `ConflictException` unless the message status is `Running`.
- Add unit tests in the chat service spec for the history filter and for the status guard.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A chat containing a failed assistant message followed by a new user message yields a claimed history with no empty-content entries.
- [ ] `completeTurn` on a `Complete` or `Failed` message throws and leaves the stored content unchanged.
- [ ] `completeTurn` and `failTurn` on a `Running` message still work.
- [ ] The new tests pass with `npm test -w backend`.

items.title: Reject queued/claimed in UpdateJobStatusDto and guard job status transitions
items.body:
## Problem
`UpdateJobStatusDto` says `'queued'/'claimed' are ... never accepted here` (`bridge/apps/backend/src/worker/dto/update-job-status.dto.ts:5-7`). The validator is `@IsEnum(JobStatus)` (line 9), so it accepts every enum value. The TypeScript union on line 10 is not checked at runtime. `WorkerService.updateStatus` (`bridge/apps/backend/src/worker/worker.service.ts:156-175`) then runs `job.status = dto.status` with no check of the current state. A late `running` report, or a `queued` or `claimed` one, can overwrite a `succeeded` or `failed` job. A `failed` report can also overwrite a `succeeded` job.

## Proposed change
- Replace `@IsEnum(JobStatus)` with `@IsIn([JobStatus.Running, JobStatus.Succeeded, JobStatus.Failed])`.
- In `updateStatus`, reject a transition out of a terminal state (`succeeded` or `failed`) with `ConflictException`.
- Add DTO validation tests and service tests for the allowed and rejected transitions.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `POST` of status `queued` or `claimed` returns 400.
- [ ] Updating a `succeeded` or `failed` job to any other status returns 409.
- [ ] The normal flow claimed -> running -> succeeded/failed is unchanged.
- [ ] Tests cover each case and pass.

items.title: Keep the worker heartbeat alive while a long job is running
items.body:
## Problem
The heartbeat is recorded only inside `WorkerService.claim` (`bridge/apps/backend/src/worker/worker.service.ts:99-105`). The staleness threshold is `STALE_AFTER_MS = 30_000` (`bridge/apps/backend/src/worker/worker-heartbeat.service.ts:17`). The worker main loop awaits `processJob` and `continue`s without polling (`worker/src/index.ts:212-215`), so no claim happens while a job runs. The job timeout defaults to 30 minutes (`worker/src/config.ts:28`). Any job longer than 30s makes the Worker page report the worker as down while it is busy.

## Proposed change
- Add a cheap heartbeat call from worker, for example a `POST` to a small heartbeat route or a claim-less ping reusing `heartbeatService.record`.
- Send it on an interval from `processJob`, for example next to the existing log flush interval, and clear the interval in `finally`.
- Add a worker test with fake timers that checks the ping fires during a long job, and a backend test for the route.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] While a job runs for longer than 30s, the heartbeat is refreshed at least every ~10s.
- [ ] The interval is cleared when the job finishes, fails or throws.
- [ ] Existing worker and backend tests still pass.

items.title: Catch DB errors in StorageController's fire-and-forget delete after download
items.body:
## Problem
After a successful download, `storage.controller.ts:89` calls `void this.storageService.delete(file);`. In `StorageService.delete` (`bridge/apps/backend/src/storage/storage.service.ts:83-91`), `await this.storedFileRepository.delete(file.id)` sits outside the `try`. Only the `unlink` is guarded. If the DB delete rejects (connection drop, pool exhaustion), the promise has no handler. On Node 22 that is an unhandled rejection, which by default terminates the process, and the relay does not clean up the file row.

## Proposed change
- At the call site, use `this.storageService.delete(file).catch((err) => this.logger.warn(...))`.
- Optionally make `delete` unlink the file even if the DB delete fails, or the reverse, and log either way.
- Add a test that a rejecting repository `delete` does not produce an unhandled rejection.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A failing `storedFileRepository.delete` during download logs a warning and does not raise an unhandled rejection.
- [ ] The download response is still sent.
- [ ] The new test passes with `npm test -w backend`.

items.title: Refresh sync's cached access token and retry once on a 401 response
items.body:
## Problem
`BridgeClient.authHeader` caches the access token for the lifetime of the client: `if (!this.accessToken) { this.accessToken = await refreshAccessToken(...) }` (`sync/src/bridgeClient.ts:69-72`). No request path clears it on a 401. Bridge access tokens are short-lived (about 15 minutes, see `bridge/apps/backend/src/auth/auth.service.ts`). Long-running commands (`agentRunner`, `gitlabWorker`, `pullIssue` polling) reuse one client, so after expiry every call fails with `Failed to list storage files (401)` until the process is restarted. This affects refresh-token login only, not API-key login. Also, `refreshAccessToken` returns `body.accessToken` without validating it (`sync/src/bridgeClient.ts:52-53`).

## Proposed change
- Wrap the fetch calls in one helper that, on a 401 when not using an API key, clears `this.accessToken`, re-runs `authHeader`, and retries once.
- Throw a clear error if the refresh response has no string `accessToken`.
- Add tests in sync with a mocked `fetch`: first call 401, refresh, second call 200.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A 401 followed by a successful refresh results in a successful retry, with exactly one retry.
- [ ] A second 401 surfaces the original error.
- [ ] API-key login never triggers the refresh path.
- [ ] A refresh body without `accessToken` fails with a descriptive error.
- [ ] `npm test` in `sync` passes.
